analysis.title: Weekly Market View: Staying diversified, adding US mega caps
key_insights: AI-related concerns weigh on equities after new US restrictions on third-country access to advanced American chips, including remote access through overseas data centres. The VIX moved back above 25.
Two event risks this week were less concerning than feared: Nvidia's Q3 revenue and earnings exceeded expectations, and Anthropic's initial public offering priced above its indicative range.

Quant models do not signal a strong buy yet. With VIX above 25 and positioning and sentiment indicators suggesting limited downside, SC sees value in US mega caps after their recent underperformance and adds them as a new opportunistic idea.

US mega caps' forward P/E has fallen well below its two-year average and the -2x standard deviation level. SC cites scale, financial strength, cash generation and potential industry consolidation as the supports.

SC expects market AI capex estimates for 2027 to be cut toward its own more conservative projections. It forecasts AI capex up 50% to USD 1.2trn in 2027, with the 2027-2030 CAGR moderating to about 12%.

Hyperscalers may manage customer checks under the new licensing rules better than smaller providers. SC favours broadening tech exposure beyond semiconductors through its US IT opportunistic idea, which includes hardware and software.

Preferred US sectors are technology, healthcare, financials and materials. Outside the US, SC likes Euro area and Japanese banks, global dividend strategies and Indian equities, which have low correlation with the AI trade.
The one-month global stock-bond correlation turned negative after more than a year, so bonds are offering more diversification during the equity drawdown.
The Fed's October minutes showed almost all officials saw further hikes, and a couple considered a larger move in December. SC expects a 25bps hike at the 8-9 December meeting.

SC is more dovish than markets on the Fed. It sees the target rate at 4.25% by end-2027 against market pricing above 4.5%, because lower oil and fading tariff effects should produce disinflation by H2 2027.
SC sees value in the 3-7 year maturity bucket and in BB-to-BBB corporate bonds. It sees the US 10-year as offering value if the yield rises above 5.25%.
DXY rose over 2% in two weeks after strong October US jobs and inflation data revived hike bets. SC calls the dollar technically overbought and expects a pullback.
Crude oil fell almost 20% this month after Republican losses in the US midterms raised prospects of Middle East de-escalation. Forward markets price US crude below USD 75/bbl by Q3 next year.

SC cut its gold targets to USD 4,000/oz (3 months) and USD 4,500/oz (12 months). Gold has dropped below the new 3-month target, and SC still sees upside from EM central bank buying and US fiscal concerns.
SC is bullish on EUR/USD and favours adding EUR gradually. It expects a rebound toward 1.11 within three weeks, citing an RSI below 30 and consolidation above 1.0950.
SC looks for an AUD/USD rebound from 0.6600 with key resistance at 0.6830. A sustained recovery needs softer US data or less hawkish Fed communication, and a stabilisation in AI sentiment.
Chinese tech Q3 earnings showed rising AI demand but heavy capex is pressuring margins and free cash flow. Share dilution is a risk, and weak consumer spending drove revenue misses.

SC expects near-term WTI to range between USD 80 and USD 90/bbl. Gulf crude flows have recovered to nearly 70% of pre-conflict levels, and US SPR inventories are down nearly 33% from pre-conflict levels.
The weekly net assessment is neutral for risk assets. Positives are strong US retail sales and ongoing peace talks. Negatives are the China slowdown and hawkish central banks.

Iran claimed several tankers hit mines near Hormuz and declared the strait closed.
Qatar said US-Iran mediation efforts are continuing.
US envoy Kushner said Russia-Ukraine peace talks are making progress, with a new multilateral meeting being prepared.
Xi and Putin pledged at the APEC summit to lead efforts toward a multipolar world order.
Republican losses in the US midterm elections raised prospects of de-escalation in the Middle East conflict. They also brought political gridlock back to Washington.

tension_points.bull_case: The forward P/E is well below its two-year average, and cash generation, scale and balance sheets favour leaders, with possible consolidation if AI capex resets.
tension_points.bear_case: Risks include a sharper slowdown, weaker returns on AI investment, regulatory pressure and concentration. New US chip restrictions could cut AI capex.
tension_points.what_invalidates: SC's quant models do not yet signal a strong buy. The report names no specific invalidation level.

tension_points.bull_case: Lower oil and fading tariff effects bring disinflation by H2 2027, so the Fed can pivot toward easing and the target rate reaches 4.25% by end-2027.
tension_points.bear_case: The October minutes showed almost all officials saw more hikes, and a couple considered a larger move in December. Strong jobs and inflation data revived hike bets.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A 10-year yield spike above 5.25% is SC's entry point for bonds, and a hotter-than-expected inflation path would undercut the disinflation view.
